passages.text: Intention is the leader of things; intention is first, they’re made by intention. If with corrupt intent you speak or act, suffering follows you, like a wheel, the ox’s foot.
passages.title: Dhammapada 1 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā,  manoseṭṭhā manomayā;  Manasā ce paduṭṭhena,  bhāsati vā karoti vā;  Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti,  cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.

passages.text: Intention is the leader of things; intention is first, they’re made by intention. If with pure intent you speak or act, happiness follows you like a shadow that never leaves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 2 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā,  manoseṭṭhā manomayā;  Manasā ce pasannena,  bhāsati vā karoti vā;  Tato naṁ sukhamanveti,  chāyāva anapāyinī.

passages.text: “They abused me, they hit me! They beat me, they robbed me!” For those who bear such a grudge, hatred is never laid to rest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 3 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ,  ajini maṁ ahāsi me;  Ye ca taṁ upanayhanti,  veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.

passages.text: “They abused me, they hit me! They beat me, they robbed me!” For those who bear no such grudge, hatred is laid to rest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 4 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ,  ajini maṁ ahāsi me;  Ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti,  veraṁ tesūpasammati.

passages.text: For never is hatred laid to rest by hate, it’s laid to rest by love: this is an ancient teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 5 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Na hi verena verāni,  sammantīdha kudācanaṁ;  Averena ca sammanti,  esa dhammo sanantano.

passages.text: When others do not understand, let us, who do understand this, restrain ourselves in this regard; for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 6 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Pare ca na vijānanti,  mayamettha yamāmase;  Ye ca tattha vijānanti,  tato sammanti medhagā.

passages.text: Those who contemplate the beautiful, their faculties unrestrained, immoderate in eating, lazy, lacking energy: Māra strikes them down like the wind, a feeble tree.
passages.title: Dhammapada 7 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ,  indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ;  Bhojanamhi cāmattaññuṁ,  kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ;  Taṁ ve pasahati māro,  vāto rukkhaṁva dubbalaṁ.

passages.text: Those who contemplate the ugly, their faculties well-restrained, eating in moderation, faithful and energetic: Māra cannot strike them down, like the wind, a rocky mountain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 8 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ,  Indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ;  Bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ,  Saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ;  Taṁ ve nappasahati māro,  Vāto selaṁva pabbataṁ.

passages.text: One who, not free of stains themselves, would wear the robe stained in ocher, bereft of self-control and truth: they are not worthy of the ocher robe.
passages.title: Dhammapada 9 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ,  yo vatthaṁ paridahissati;  Apeto damasaccena,  na so kāsāvamarahati.

passages.text: One who’s purged all their stains, steady in ethics, possessed of self-control and of truth, they are truly worthy of the ocher robe.
passages.title: Dhammapada 10 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Yo ca vantakasāvassa,  sīlesu susamāhito;  Upeto damasaccena,  sa ve kāsāvamarahati.

passages.text: Thinking the inessential is essential, seeing the essential as inessential; they don’t realize the essential, for wrong thoughts are their habitat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 11 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Asāre sāramatino,  sāre cāsāradassino;  Te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti,  micchāsaṅkappagocarā.

passages.text: Having known the essential as essential, and the inessential as inessential; they realize the essential, for right thoughts are their habitat.
passages.title: Dhammapada 12 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Sārañca sārato ñatvā,  asārañca asārato;  Te sāraṁ adhigacchanti,  sammāsaṅkappagocarā.

passages.text: Just as rain seeps into a poorly roofed house, lust seeps into an undeveloped mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 13 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ,  vuṭṭhī samativijjhati;  Evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ,  rāgo samativijjhati.

passages.text: Just as rain doesn’t seep into a well roofed house, lust doesn’t seep into a well developed mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 14 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Yathā agāraṁ suchannaṁ,  vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati;  Evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ,  rāgo na samativijjhati.

passages.text: Here they grieve, hereafter they grieve, an evildoer grieves in both places. They grieve and fret, seeing their own corrupt deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 15 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Idha socati pecca socati,  Pāpakārī ubhayattha socati;  So socati so vihaññati,  Disvā kammakiliṭṭhamattano.

passages.text: Here they rejoice, hereafter they rejoice, one who does good rejoices in both places. They rejoice and celebrate, seeing their own pure deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 16 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Idha modati pecca modati,  Katapuñño ubhayattha modati;  So modati so pamodati,  Disvā kammavisuddhimattano.

passages.text: Here they’re tormented, hereafter they’re tormented, an evildoer is tormented in both places. They’re tormented thinking of bad things they’ve done; when gone to a bad place, they’re tormented all the more.
passages.title: Dhammapada 17 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Idha tappati pecca tappati,  Pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati;  “Pāpaṁ me katan”ti tappati,  Bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.

passages.text: Here they delight, hereafter they delight, one who does good delights in both places. They delight thinking of good things they’ve done; when gone to a good place, they delight all the more.
passages.title: Dhammapada 18 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Idha nandati pecca nandati,  Katapuñño ubhayattha nandati;  “Puññaṁ me katan”ti nandati,  Bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.

passages.text: Much though they may recite scripture, if a negligent person does not apply them, then, like a cowherd who counts the cattle of others, they miss out on the blessings of the ascetic life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 19 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Bahumpi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno,  Na takkaro hoti naro pamatto;  Gopova gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ,  Na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.

passages.text: Little though they may recite scripture, if they live in line with the teaching, having given up greed, hate, and delusion, with deep understanding and heart well freed, not grasping to this life or the next, they share in the blessings of the ascetic life.
passages.title: Dhammapada 20 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 1–20 · 1. Pairs
passages.original: Appampi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno,  Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī;  Rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohaṁ,  Sammappajāno suvimuttacitto;  Anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā,  Sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.

passages.text: Better than a thousand meaningless sayings is a single meaningful saying, hearing which brings you peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 100 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Sahassamapi ce vācā,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: Better than a thousand meaningless verses is a single meaningful verse, hearing which brings you peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 101 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Sahassamapi ce gāthā,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: Better than reciting a hundred meaningless verses is a single saying of Dhamma, hearing which brings you peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 102 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca gāthā sataṁ bhāse,  anatthapadasaṁhitā;  Ekaṁ dhammapadaṁ seyyo,  yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

passages.text: The supreme conqueror is not he who conquers a million men in battle, but he who conquers a single man: himself.
passages.title: Dhammapada 103 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena,  saṅgāme mānuse jine;  Ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ,  sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.

passages.text: It is surely better to conquer oneself than all those other folk. When a person has tamed themselves, always living restrained,
passages.title: Dhammapada 104 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo,  yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā;  Attadantassa posassa,  niccaṁ saññatacārino.

passages.text: no god nor centaur, nor Māra nor divinity, can undo the victory of such a personage.
passages.title: Dhammapada 105 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Neva devo na gandhabbo,  na māro saha brahmunā;  Jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā,  tathārūpassa jantuno.

passages.text: Rather than a thousandfold sacrifice, every month for a full century, it’s better to honor for a single hour one who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.
passages.title: Dhammapada 106 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Māse māse sahassena,  yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ;  Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ,  muhuttamapi pūjaye;  Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo,  yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.

passages.text: Rather than serve the sacred flame in the forest for a hundred years, it’s better to honor for a single hour a personage who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.
passages.title: Dhammapada 107 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu,  aggiṁ paricare vane;  Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ,  muhuttamapi pūjaye;  Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo,  yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.

passages.text: Whatever sacrifice or offering in the world a seeker of merit may make for a year, none of it is worth a quarter of bowing to the sincere.
passages.title: Dhammapada 108 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ va hutaṁ va loke,  Saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho;  Sabbampi taṁ na catubhāgameti,  Abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.

passages.text: For one in the habit of bowing, always honoring the elders, four blessings grow: lifespan, beauty, happiness, and strength.
passages.title: Dhammapada 109 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Abhivādanasīlissa,  niccaṁ vuḍḍhāpacāyino;  Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti,  āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.

passages.text: Better to live a single day ethical and absorbed in meditation than to live a hundred years unethical and lacking immersion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 110 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  dussīlo asamāhito;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  sīlavantassa jhāyino.

passages.text: Better to live a single day wise and absorbed in meditation than to live a hundred years witless and lacking immersion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 111 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  duppañño asamāhito;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  paññavantassa jhāyino.

passages.text: Better to live a single day energetic and strong, than to live a hundred years lazy and lacking energy.
passages.title: Dhammapada 112 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  kusīto hīnavīriyo;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  vīriyamārabhato daḷhaṁ.

passages.text: Better to live a single day seeing rise and fall than to live a hundred years blind to rise and fall.
passages.title: Dhammapada 113 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato udayabbayaṁ.

passages.text: Better to live a single day seeing the state free of death than to live a hundred years blind to the state free of death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 114 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato amataṁ padaṁ.

passages.text: Better to live a single day seeing the supreme teaching than to live a hundred years blind to the supreme teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 115 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 100–115 · 8. The Thousands
passages.original: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve,  apassaṁ dhammamuttamaṁ;  Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo,  passato dhammamuttamaṁ.

passages.text: Rush to do good, shield your mind from evil; for when you’re slow to do good, your thoughts delight in wickedness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 116 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe,  pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye;  Dandhañhi karoto puññaṁ,  pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.

passages.text: If you do something bad, don’t do it again and again, don’t set your heart on it, for piling up evil is suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 117 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Pāpañce puriso kayirā,  Na naṁ kayirā punappunaṁ;  Na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha,  Dukkho pāpassa uccayo.

passages.text: If you do something good, do it again and again, set your heart on it, for piling up goodness is joyful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 118 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Puññañce puriso kayirā,  kayirā naṁ punappunaṁ;  Tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha,  sukho puññassa uccayo.

passages.text: Even the wicked see good things, so long as their wickedness has not ripened. But as soon as that wickedness ripens, then the wicked see wicked things.
passages.title: Dhammapada 119 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Pāpopi passati bhadraṁ,  Yāva pāpaṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ,  Atha pāpo pāpāni passati.

passages.text: Even the good see wicked things, so long as their goodness has not ripened. But as soon as that goodness ripens, then the good see good things.
passages.title: Dhammapada 120 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Bhadropi passati pāpaṁ,  Yāva bhadraṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ,  Atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.

passages.text: Think not lightly of evil, that it won’t come back to you. The pot is filled with water falling drop by drop; the fool is filled with wickedness piled up bit by bit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 121 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Māvamaññetha pāpassa,  na mantaṁ āgamissati;  Udabindunipātena,  udakumbhopi pūrati;  Bālo pūrati pāpassa,  thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.

passages.text: Think not lightly of goodness, that it won’t come back to you. The pot is filled with water falling drop by drop; the attentive one is filled with goodness piled up bit by bit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 122 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Māvamaññetha puññassa,  na mandaṁ āgamissati;  Udabindunipātena,  udakumbhopi pūrati;  Dhīro pūrati puññassa,  thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.

passages.text: Avoid wickedness, as a merchant with rich cargo and small escort would avoid a dangerous road, or one who loves life would avoid drinking poison.
passages.title: Dhammapada 123 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Vāṇijova bhayaṁ maggaṁ,  appasattho mahaddhano;  Visaṁ jīvitukāmova,  pāpāni parivajjaye.

passages.text: You can carry poison in your hand if it has no wound, for poison does not infect without a wound; nothing bad happens unless you do bad.
passages.title: Dhammapada 124 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa,  hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ;  Nābbaṇaṁ visamanveti,  natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.

passages.text: Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong, a pure man who has not a blemish, the evil backfires on the fool, like fine dust thrown upwind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 125 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati,  Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa;  Tameva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ,  Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁva khitto.

passages.text: Some are born in a womb; evildoers go to hell; the virtuous go to heaven; the undefiled are fully extinguished.
passages.title: Dhammapada 126 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Gabbhameke uppajjanti,  nirayaṁ pāpakammino;  Saggaṁ sugatino yanti,  parinibbanti anāsavā.

passages.text: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet to escape your wicked deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 127 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,  Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa;  Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso,  Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.

passages.text: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet where you won’t be vanquished by death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 128 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 116–128 · 9. Wickedness
passages.original: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,  Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa;  Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso,  Yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasaheyya maccu.

passages.text: All tremble at the rod, all fear death. Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.
passages.title: Dhammapada 129 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa,  sabbe bhāyanti maccuno;  Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā,  na haneyya na ghātaye.

passages.text: All tremble at the rod, all love life. Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.
passages.title: Dhammapada 130 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa,  sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ;  Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā,  na haneyya na ghātaye.

passages.text: Creatures love happiness, so if you harm them with a stick in search of your own happiness, after death you won’t find happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 131 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni,  yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati;  Attano sukhamesāno,  pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Creatures love happiness, so if you don’t harm them with a stick in search of your own happiness, after death you will find happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 132 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni,  yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati;  Attano sukhamesāno,  pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Don’t speak harshly, they may speak harshly back. For aggressive speech is painful, and the rod may spring back on you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 133 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci,  vuttā paṭivadeyyu taṁ;  Dukkhā hi sārambhakathā,  paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu taṁ.

passages.text: If you still yourself like a broken gong, you reach extinguishment and know no conflict.
passages.title: Dhammapada 134 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Sace neresi attānaṁ,  kaṁso upahato yathā;  Esa pattosi nibbānaṁ,  sārambho te na vijjati.

passages.text: As a cowherd drives the cows to pasture with the rod, so too old age and death drive life from living beings.
passages.title: Dhammapada 135 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo,  gāvo pājeti gocaraṁ;  Evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca,  āyuṁ pājenti pāṇinaṁ.

passages.text: The fool does not understand the evil that they do. But because of those deeds, that simpleton is tormented as if burnt by fire.
passages.title: Dhammapada 136 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Atha pāpāni kammāni,  karaṁ bālo na bujjhati;  Sehi kammehi dummedho,  aggidaḍḍhova tappati.

passages.text: One who violently attacks the peaceful and the innocent swiftly falls to one of ten bad states:
passages.title: Dhammapada 137 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu,  appaduṭṭhesu dussati;  Dasannamaññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ,  khippameva nigacchati.

passages.text: harsh pain; loss; the breakup of the body; serious illness; mental distress;
passages.title: Dhammapada 138 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Vedanaṁ pharusaṁ jāniṁ,  sarīrassa va bhedanaṁ;  Garukaṁ vāpi ābādhaṁ,  cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe.

passages.text: hazards from rulers; vicious slander; loss of kin; destruction of wealth;
passages.title: Dhammapada 139 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Rājato vā upasaggaṁ,  Abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ;  Parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ,  Bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ.

passages.text: or else their home is consumed by fire. When their body breaks up, that witless person is reborn in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 140 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Atha vāssa agārāni,  aggi ḍahati pāvako;  Kāyassa bhedā duppañño,  nirayaṁ sopapajjati.

passages.text: Not nudity, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting, nor lying on bare ground, nor wearing dust and dirt, or squatting on the heels, will cleanse a mortal not free of doubt.
passages.title: Dhammapada 141 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā,  Nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā;  Rajojallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ,  Sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.

passages.text: Dressed up they may be, but if they live well— peaceful, tamed, committed to the spiritual path, having laid aside violence toward all creatures— they are a brahmin, an ascetic, a mendicant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 142 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Alaṅkato cepi samaṁ careyya,  Santo danto niyato brahmacārī;  Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ,  So brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.

passages.text: Can a person constrained by conscience be found in the world? Who shies away from blame, like a fine horse from the whip?
passages.title: Dhammapada 143 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Hirīnisedho puriso,  koci lokasmi vijjati;  Yo niddaṁ apabodheti,  asso bhadro kasāmiva.

passages.text: Like a fine horse under the whip, be keen and full of urgency. With faith, ethics, and energy, immersion, and investigation of principles, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, mindful, give up this vast suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 144 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho,  Ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha;  Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca,  Samādhinā dhammavinicchayena ca;  Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā,  Jahissatha dukkhamidaṁ anappakaṁ.

passages.text: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, those true to their vows tame themselves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 145 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 129–145 · 10. The Rod
passages.original: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā,  Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ;  Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā,  Attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.

passages.text: What is joy, what is laughter, when the flames are ever burning? Swathed in darkness, would you not seek a light?
passages.title: Dhammapada 146 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Ko nu hāso kimānando,  niccaṁ pajjalite sati;  Andhakārena onaddhā,  padīpaṁ na gavesatha.

passages.text: See this fancy puppet, a body built of sores, diseased, obsessed over, in which nothing lasts at all.
passages.title: Dhammapada 147 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ,  arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ;  Āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ,  yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.

passages.text: This body is decrepit and frail, a nest of disease. This foul carcass falls apart, for life ends in death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 148 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Parijiṇṇamidaṁ rūpaṁ,  roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ;  Bhijjati pūtisandeho,  maraṇantañhi jīvitaṁ.

passages.text: These dove-grey bones are tossed away like dried gourds in the autumn— what joy is there in such a sight?
passages.title: Dhammapada 149 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Yānimāni apatthāni,  alābūneva sārade;  Kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni,  tāni disvāna kā rati.

passages.text: In this city built of bones, plastered with flesh and blood, old age and death are stashed away, along with conceit and contempt.
passages.title: Dhammapada 150 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ,  maṁsalohitalepanaṁ;  Yattha jarā ca maccu ca,  māno makkho ca ohito.

passages.text: Fancy chariots of kings wear out, and even this body gets old. But the truth of the good never gets old— so the good proclaim to the good.
passages.title: Dhammapada 151 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā,  Atho sarīrampi jaraṁ upeti;  Satañca dhammo na jaraṁ upeti,  Santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.

passages.text: A person of little learning ages like an ox— their flesh grows, but not their wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 152 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Appassutāyaṁ puriso,  balībaddhova jīrati;  Maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti,  paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Transmigrating through countless rebirths, I’ve journeyed without reward, searching for the house-builder; painful is birth again and again.
passages.title: Dhammapada 153 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ,  sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ;  Gahakāraṁ gavesanto,  dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.

passages.text: I’ve seen you, house-builder! You won’t build a house again! Your rafters are all broken, your roof-peak demolished. The mind, set on demolition, has reached the end of cravings.
passages.title: Dhammapada 154 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi,  puna gehaṁ na kāhasi;  Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā,  gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhataṁ;  Visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ,  taṇhānaṁ khayamajjhagā.

passages.text: When young they spurned the spiritual path and failed to earn any wealth. Now they brood like old cranes in a pond bereft of fish.
passages.title: Dhammapada 155 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ,  aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ;  Jiṇṇakoñcāva jhāyanti,  khīṇamaccheva pallale.

passages.text: When young they spurned the spiritual path and failed to earn any wealth. Now they lie like spent arrows, bemoaning over things past.
passages.title: Dhammapada 156 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 146–156 · 11. Old Age
passages.original: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ,  aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ;  Senti cāpātikhīṇāva,  purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.

passages.text: If you knew your self as beloved, you’d look after it so well. In one of the night’s three watches, an astute person would remain alert.
passages.title: Dhammapada 157 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attānañce piyaṁ jaññā,  rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ;  Tiṇṇaṁ aññataraṁ yāmaṁ,  paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: The astute would avoid being corrupted by first grounding themselves in what is suitable, and then instructing others.
passages.title: Dhammapada 158 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attānameva paṭhamaṁ,  patirūpe nivesaye;  Athaññamanusāseyya,  na kilisseyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: If one were to treat oneself as one instructs another, the well-tamed indeed would tame: for the self, it seems, is hard to tame.
passages.title: Dhammapada 159 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attānañce tathā kayirā,  yathāññamanusāsati;  Sudanto vata dametha,  attā hi kira duddamo.

passages.text: One is indeed the lord of oneself, for who else would be one’s lord? By means of a well-tamed self, one gains a lord that’s rare indeed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 160 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attā hi attano nātho,  ko hi nātho paro siyā;  Attanā hi sudantena,  nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.

passages.text: For the evil that is done by oneself, born and produced in oneself, grinds down a simpleton, as diamond grinds a lesser gem.
passages.title: Dhammapada 161 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ,  Attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ;  Abhimatthati dummedhaṁ,  Vajiraṁvasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.

passages.text: One choked by immorality, as a sal tree by a creeper, does to themselves what a foe only wishes.
passages.title: Dhammapada 162 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Yassa accantadussilyaṁ,  māluvā sālamivotthataṁ;  Karoti so tathattānaṁ,  yathā naṁ icchatī diso.

passages.text: It’s easy to do bad things harmful to oneself, but good things that are helpful are the hardest things to do.
passages.title: Dhammapada 163 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Sukarāni asādhūni,  attano ahitāni ca;  Yaṁ ve hitañca sādhuñca,  taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.

passages.text: On account of wicked views— scorning the guidance of the perfected ones, the noble ones living righteously— the idiot begets their own self’s demise, like the bamboo bearing fruit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 164 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ,  ariyānaṁ dhammajīvinaṁ;  Paṭikkosati dummedho,  diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ;  Phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva,  attaghātāya phallati.

passages.text: For it is by oneself that evil’s done, one is corrupted by oneself. It’s by oneself that evil’s not done, one is purified by oneself. Purity and impurity are personal matters, no one can purify another.
passages.title: Dhammapada 165 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ,  attanā saṅkilissati;  Attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ,  attanāva visujjhati;  Suddhī asuddhi paccattaṁ,  nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.

passages.text: Never neglect what is good for yourself for the sake of another, however great. Knowing well what is good for yourself, be intent upon your heart’s goal.
passages.title: Dhammapada 166 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 157–166 · 12. The Self
passages.original: Attadatthaṁ paratthena,  bahunāpi na hāpaye;  Attadatthamabhiññāya,  sadatthapasuto siyā.

passages.text: Don’t resort to lowly things, don’t abide in negligence, don’t resort to wrong views, don’t perpetuate the world.
passages.title: Dhammapada 167 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya,  pamādena na saṁvase;  Micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya,  na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.

passages.text: Get up, don’t be heedless, live by principle, with good conduct. For one of good conduct sleeps at ease, in this world and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 168 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya,  dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care;  Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: Live by principle, with good conduct, don’t conduct yourself badly. For one of good conduct sleeps at ease, in this world and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 169 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ,  na naṁ duccaritaṁ care;  Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: Look upon the world as a bubble or a mirage, then the King of Death won’t see you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 170 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Yathā pubbuḷakaṁ passe,  yathā passe marīcikaṁ;  Evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ,  maccurājā na passati.

passages.text: Come, see this world decked out like a fancy royal chariot. Here fools founder, but the discerning are not chained.
passages.title: Dhammapada 171 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ,  cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ;  Yattha bālā visīdanti,  natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.

passages.text: He who once was heedless, but turned to heedfulness, shines upon this world like the moon freed from clouds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 172 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā,  pacchā so nappamajjati;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.

passages.text: Someone whose bad deed is supplanted by the good, shines upon this world, like the moon freed from clouds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 173 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ,  kusalena pidhīyati;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.

passages.text: Blind is the world, few are those who clearly see. Only a handful go to heaven, like a bird freed from a net.
passages.title: Dhammapada 174 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko,  tanukettha vipassati;  Sakuṇo jālamuttova,  appo saggāya gacchati.

passages.text: Swans fly by the sun’s path, psychic sages fly through space. The attentive leave the world, having vanquished Māra with his legions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 175 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti,  ākāse yanti iddhiyā;  Nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā,  jetvā māraṁ savāhiniṁ.

passages.text: When a personage, spurning the hereafter, transgresses in just one thing— lying— there is no evil they would not do.
passages.title: Dhammapada 176 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa,  musāvādissa jantuno;  Vitiṇṇaparalokassa,  natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.

passages.text: The miserly don’t ascend to heaven, it takes a fool to not praise giving. The attentive celebrate giving, and so find happiness in the hereafter.
passages.title: Dhammapada 177 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti,  Bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ;  Dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno,  Teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.

passages.text: The fruit of stream-entry is better than being the one king of the earth, than going to heaven, than lordship over all the world.
passages.title: Dhammapada 178 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 167–178 · 13. The World
passages.original: Pathabyā ekarajjena,  saggassa gamanena vā;  Sabbalokādhipaccena,  sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.

passages.text: He whose victory may not be undone, a victory unrivaled in all the world; by what track would you trace that Buddha, who leaves no track in his infinite range?
passages.title: Dhammapada 179 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati,  Jitaṁ yassa noyāti koci loke;  Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ,  Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.

passages.text: Of craving, the weaver, the clinger, he has none: so where can he be traced? By what track would you trace that Buddha, who leaves no track in his infinite range?
passages.title: Dhammapada 180 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Yassa jālinī visattikā,  Taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave;  Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ,  Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.

passages.text: The attentive intent on absorption, who love the peace of renunciation, the Buddhas, ever mindful, are envied by even the gods.
passages.title: Dhammapada 181 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā,  nekkhammūpasame ratā;  Devāpi tesaṁ pihayanti,  sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.

passages.text: It’s hard to gain a human birth; the life of mortals is hard; it’s hard to hear the true teaching; the arising of Buddhas is hard.
passages.title: Dhammapada 182 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho,  kicchaṁ maccāna jīvitaṁ;  Kicchaṁ saddhammassavanaṁ,  kiccho buddhānamuppādo.

passages.text: Not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind: this is the instruction of the Buddhas.
passages.title: Dhammapada 183 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ,  kusalassa upasampadā;  Sacittapariyodapanaṁ,  etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.

passages.text: Patient acceptance is the ultimate fervor. Extinguishment is the ultimate, say the Buddhas. No true renunciate injures another, nor does an ascetic hurt another.
passages.title: Dhammapada 184 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā,  Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti buddhā;  Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī,  Na samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.

passages.text: Not speaking ill nor doing harm; restraint in the monastic code; moderation in eating; staying in remote lodgings; commitment to the higher mind— this is the instruction of the Buddhas.
passages.title: Dhammapada 185 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Anūpavādo anūpaghāto,  Pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro;  Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ,  Pantañca sayanāsanaṁ;  Adhicitte ca āyogo,  Etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.

passages.text: Even if it were raining money, you’d not be sated in sensual pleasures. An astute person understands that sensual pleasures offer little gratification and much suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 186 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Na kahāpaṇavassena,  titti kāmesu vijjati;  Appassādā dukhā kāmā,  iti viññāya paṇḍito.

passages.text: Thus they find no delight even in celestial pleasures. A disciple of the fully awakened Buddha delights in the ending of craving.
passages.title: Dhammapada 187 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Api dibbesu kāmesu,  ratiṁ so nādhigacchati;  Taṇhakkhayarato hoti,  sammāsambuddhasāvako.

passages.text: So many go for refuge to mountains and forest groves, to shrines in tended parks; those people are driven by fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 188 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti,  pabbatāni vanāni ca;  Ārāmarukkhacetyāni,  manussā bhayatajjitā.

passages.text: But such refuge is no sanctuary, it is no supreme refuge. By going to that refuge, you’re not released from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 189 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ,  netaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ;  Netaṁ saraṇamāgamma,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: One gone for refuge to the Buddha, to his teaching and to the Saṅgha, sees the four noble truths with right understanding:
passages.title: Dhammapada 190 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca,  saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gato;  Cattāri ariyasaccāni,  sammappaññāya passati.

passages.text: suffering, suffering’s origin, suffering’s transcendence, and the noble eightfold path that leads to the stilling of suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 191 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ,  dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ;  Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,  dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.

passages.text: Such refuge is a sanctuary, it is the supreme refuge. By going to that refuge, you’re released from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 192 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ,  etaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ;  Etaṁ saraṇamāgamma,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: It’s hard to find a thoroughbred man: they’re not born just anywhere. A family where that attentive one is born prospers in happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 193 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Dullabho purisājañño,  na so sabbattha jāyati;  Yattha so jāyati dhīro,  taṁ kulaṁ sukhamedhati.

passages.text: Happy, the arising of Buddhas! Happy, the teaching of Dhamma! Happy is the harmony of the Saṅgha, and the striving of the harmonious is happy.
passages.title: Dhammapada 194 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Sukho buddhānamuppādo,  sukhā saddhammadesanā;  Sukhā saṅghassa sāmaggī,  samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.

passages.text: When a person venerates the worthy— the Buddha or his disciple, who have transcended proliferation, and have left behind grief and lamentation,
passages.title: Dhammapada 195 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Pūjārahe pūjayato,  buddhe yadi va sāvake;  Papañcasamatikkante,  tiṇṇasokapariddave.

passages.text: quenched, fearing nothing from any quarter— the merit of one venerating such as these, cannot be calculated by anyone, saying it is just this much.
passages.title: Dhammapada 196 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 179–196 · 14. The Buddhas
passages.original: Te tādise pūjayato,  nibbute akutobhaye;  Na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ,  imettamapi kenaci.

passages.text: Let us live so very happily, loving among the hostile. Among hostile humans, let us live with love.
passages.title: Dhammapada 197 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  verinesu averino;  Verinesu manussesu,  viharāma averino.

passages.text: Let us live so very happily, healthy among the ailing. Among ailing humans let us live healthily.
passages.title: Dhammapada 198 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  āturesu anāturā;  Āturesu manussesu,  viharāma anāturā.

passages.text: Let us live so very happily, content among the greedy. Among greedy humans, let us live content.
passages.title: Dhammapada 199 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  ussukesu anussukā;  Ussukesu manussesu,  viharāma anussukā.

passages.text: Let us live so very happily, we who have nothing. We shall feed on rapture, like the gods of sublime luminosity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 200 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma,  yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ;  Pītibhakkhā bhavissāma,  devā ābhassarā yathā.

passages.text: Victory breeds enmity; the defeated sleep badly. The peaceful sleep at ease, having left victory and defeat behind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 201 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati,  dukkhaṁ seti parājito;  Upasanto sukhaṁ seti,  hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.

passages.text: There is no fire like greed, no crime like hate, no suffering like the aggregates, no bliss beyond peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 202 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Natthi rāgasamo aggi,  Natthi dosasamo kali;  Natthi khandhasamā dukkhā,  Natthi santiparaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Hunger is the worst illness, conditions are the worst suffering. When one has known this as it is, extinguishment is the ultimate happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 203 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Jighacchāparamā rogā,  saṅkhāraparamā dukhā;  Etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ,  nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Health is the ultimate blessing; contentment, the ultimate wealth; trust is the ultimate family; extinguishment, the ultimate happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 204 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Ārogyaparamā lābhā,  Santuṭṭhiparamaṁ dhanaṁ;  Vissāsaparamā ñāti,  Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Having drunk the nectar of seclusion and the nectar of peace— free of stress, free of evil, drink the joyous nectar of truth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 205 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Pavivekarasaṁ pitvā,  rasaṁ upasamassa ca;  Niddaro hoti nippāpo,  dhammapītirasaṁ pivaṁ.

passages.text: It’s good to see the noble ones, staying with them is always good. Were you not to see fools, you’d always be happy.
passages.title: Dhammapada 206 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Sāhu dassanamariyānaṁ,  sannivāso sadā sukho;  Adassanena bālānaṁ,  niccameva sukhī siyā.

passages.text: For one who consorts with fools grieves long. Painful is living with fools, like being stuck with your enemy. Happy is living with an attentive one, like meeting with your kin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 207 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Bālasaṅgatacārī hi,  dīghamaddhāna socati;  Dukkho bālehi saṁvāso,  amitteneva sabbadā;  Dhīro ca sukhasaṁvāso,  ñātīnaṁva samāgamo.

passages.text: Therefore: An attentive one, wise and learned, a behemoth of virtue, true to their vows, noble: follow a true and intelligent person such as this, as the moon tracks the path of the stars.
passages.title: Dhammapada 208 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 197–208 · 15. Happiness
passages.original: Tasmā hi— Dhīrañca paññañca bahussutañca,  Dhorayhasīlaṁ vatavantamariyaṁ;  Taṁ tādisaṁ sappurisaṁ sumedhaṁ,  Bhajetha nakkhattapathaṁva candimā.

passages.text: Applying yourself where you ought not, neglecting what you should be doing, forgetting your goal, you cling to what you hold dear, jealous of those devoted to their heart’s goal.
passages.title: Dhammapada 209 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Ayoge yuñjamattānaṁ,  yogasmiñca ayojayaṁ;  Atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī,  pihetattānuyoginaṁ.

passages.text: Don’t ever get too close to those you like or dislike. For not seeing the liked is suffering, and so is seeing the disliked.
passages.title: Dhammapada 210 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Mā piyehi samāgañchi,  appiyehi kudācanaṁ;  Piyānaṁ adassanaṁ dukkhaṁ,  appiyānañca dassanaṁ.

passages.text: Therefore don’t hold anything dear, for it’s bad to lose those you love. No ties are found in they who hold nothing loved or loathed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 211 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Tasmā piyaṁ na kayirātha,  piyāpāyo hi pāpako;  Ganthā tesaṁ na vijjanti,  yesaṁ natthi piyāppiyaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow springs from what we hold dear, fear springs from what we hold dear; one free from holding anything dear has no sorrow, let alone fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 212 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Piyato jāyatī soko,  piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Piyato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow springs from attachment, fear springs from attachment; one free from attachment has no sorrow, let alone fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 213 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Pemato jāyatī soko,  pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Pemato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow springs from relishing, fear springs from relishing; one free from relishing has no sorrow, let alone fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 214 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Ratiyā jāyatī soko,  ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Ratiyā vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow springs from desire, fear springs from desire; one free from desire has no sorrow, let alone fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 215 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Kāmato jāyatī soko,  kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Kāmato vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Sorrow springs from craving, fear springs from craving; one free from craving has no sorrow, let alone fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 216 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko,  taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ;  Taṇhāya vippamuttassa,  natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.

passages.text: One accomplished in virtue and vision, firmly principled, and truthful, doing oneself what ought be done: that’s who the people love.
passages.title: Dhammapada 217 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Sīladassanasampannaṁ,  dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ;  Attano kamma kubbānaṁ,  taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.

passages.text: One eager to realize the ineffable would be filled with awareness. Their mind not bound to pleasures of sense, they’re said to be heading upstream.
passages.title: Dhammapada 218 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Chandajāto anakkhāte,  Manasā ca phuṭo siyā;  Kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto,  Uddhaṁsototi vuccati.

passages.text: When a man returns safely after a long time spent abroad, family, friends, and loved ones celebrate his return.
passages.title: Dhammapada 219 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ,  dūrato sotthimāgataṁ;  Ñātimittā suhajjā ca,  abhinandanti āgataṁ.

passages.text: Just so, when one who has done good goes from this world to the next, their good deeds receive them there, as family welcomes home one they love.
passages.title: Dhammapada 220 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 209–220 · 16. The Beloved
passages.original: Tatheva katapuññampi,  asmā lokā paraṁ gataṁ;  Puññāni paṭigaṇhanti,  piyaṁ ñātīva āgataṁ.

passages.text: Heedfulness is the state free of death; heedlessness is the state of death. The heedful do not die, while the heedless are like the dead.
passages.title: Dhammapada 21 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Appamādo amatapadaṁ,  pamādo maccuno padaṁ;  Appamattā na mīyanti,  ye pamattā yathā matā.

passages.text: Understanding this distinction when it comes to heedfulness, the astute rejoice in heedfulness, happy in the noble ones’ domain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 22 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Evaṁ visesato ñatvā,  appamādamhi paṇḍitā;  Appamāde pamodanti,  ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.

passages.text: They who regularly meditate, always staunchly vigorous; the attentive realize extinguishment, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
passages.title: Dhammapada 23 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Te jhāyino sātatikā,  niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā;  Phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṁ,  yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.

passages.text: For the hard-working and mindful, pure of deed and attentive, restrained, living righteously, and diligent, their reputation only grows.
passages.title: Dhammapada 24 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato,  Sucikammassa nisammakārino;  Saññatassa dhammajīvino,  Appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.

passages.text: By hard work and diligence, by restraint and by self-control, a smart person would build an island that the floods cannot overflow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 25 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Uṭṭhānenappamādena,  saṁyamena damena ca;  Dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī,  yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.

passages.text: Fools and simpletons devote themselves to negligence. But the wise protect diligence as their best treasure.
passages.title: Dhammapada 26 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Pamādamanuyuñjanti,  bālā dummedhino janā;  Appamādañca medhāvī,  dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁva rakkhati.

passages.text: Don’t devote yourself to negligence, or delight in erotic intimacy. For if you’re diligent and meditate, you’ll attain abundant happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 27 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha,  mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ;  Appamatto hi jhāyanto,  pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: When the astute dispel negligence by means of diligence, ascending the palace of wisdom, sorrowless, they behold this generation of sorrow, as an attentive one on a mountain top beholds the fools below.
passages.title: Dhammapada 28 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Pamādaṁ appamādena,  yadā nudati paṇḍito;  Paññāpāsādamāruyha,  asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ;  Pabbataṭṭhova bhūmaṭṭhe,  dhīro bāle avekkhati.

passages.text: Heedful among the heedless, wide awake while others sleep— a true sage leaves them behind, like a swift horse passing a feeble.
passages.title: Dhammapada 29 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Appamatto pamattesu,  suttesu bahujāgaro;  Abalassaṁva sīghasso,  hitvā yāti sumedhaso.

passages.text: Maghavā became chief of the gods by means of diligence. People praise diligence, while negligence is always deplored.
passages.title: Dhammapada 30 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Appamādena maghavā,  devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato;  Appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti,  pamādo garahito sadā.

passages.text: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— advances like fire, burning up fetters big and small.
passages.title: Dhammapada 31 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Appamādarato bhikkhu,  pamāde bhayadassi vā;  Saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ thūlaṁ,  ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.

passages.text: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— such a one can’t decline, and has drawn near to extinguishment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 32 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 21–32 · 2. Diligence
passages.original: Appamādarato bhikkhu,  pamāde bhayadassi vā;  Abhabbo parihānāya,  nibbānasseva santike.

passages.text: Give up anger, get rid of conceit, and escape every fetter. Sufferings don’t befall one who has nothing, not clinging to name and form.
passages.title: Dhammapada 221 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Kodhaṁ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṁ,  Saṁyojanaṁ sabbamatikkameyya;  Taṁ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṁ,  Akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.

passages.text: When anger surges like a lurching chariot, keep it in check. That’s what I call a charioteer; others just hold the reins.
passages.title: Dhammapada 222 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ,  rathaṁ bhantaṁva vāraye;  Tamahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi,  rasmiggāho itaro jano.

passages.text: Defeat anger with kindness, villainy with virtue, stinginess with giving, and lies with truth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 223 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ,  asādhuṁ sādhunā jine;  Jine kadariyaṁ dānena,  saccenālikavādinaṁ.

passages.text: Speak the truth, do not be angry, and give when asked, if only a little. By these three means, you may enter the presence of the gods.
passages.title: Dhammapada 224 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Saccaṁ bhaṇe na kujjheyya,  dajjā appampi yācito;  Etehi tīhi ṭhānehi,  gacche devāna santike.

passages.text: Those harmless sages, always restrained in body, go to the state that does not pass, where there is no sorrow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 225 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo,  niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā;  Te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ,  yattha gantvā na socare.

passages.text: Always wakeful, practicing night and day, focused only on extinguishment, their defilements come to an end.
passages.title: Dhammapada 226 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ,  ahorattānusikkhinaṁ;  Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ,  atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.

passages.text: It’s always been this way, Atula, it’s not just today. They blame you when you’re silent, they blame you when you speak a lot, and even when you speak just right: no one in the world escapes blame.
passages.title: Dhammapada 227 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Porāṇametaṁ atula,  netaṁ ajjatanāmiva;  Nindanti tuṇhimāsīnaṁ,  nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ;  Mitabhāṇimpi nindanti,  natthi loke anindito.

passages.text: There never was, nor will be, nor is there today, someone who is wholly praised or wholly blamed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 228 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Na cāhu na ca bhavissati,  na cetarahi vijjati;  Ekantaṁ nindito poso,  ekantaṁ vā pasaṁsito.

passages.text: If, after watching them day in day out, discerning people praise that sage of impeccable conduct, endowed with ethics and wisdom;
passages.title: Dhammapada 229 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Yañce viññū pasaṁsanti,  anuvicca suve suve;  Acchiddavuttiṁ medhāviṁ,  paññāsīlasamāhitaṁ.

passages.text: like a pendant of Black Plum River gold, who is worthy to criticize them? Even the gods praise them, and by the Divinity, too, they’re praised.
passages.title: Dhammapada 230 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Nikkhaṁ jambonadasseva,  ko taṁ ninditumarahati;  Devāpi naṁ pasaṁsanti,  brahmunāpi pasaṁsito.

passages.text: Guard against ill-tempered deeds, be restrained in body. Giving up bad bodily conduct, conduct yourself well in body.
passages.title: Dhammapada 231 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya,  kāyena saṁvuto siyā;  Kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā,  kāyena sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: Guard against ill-tempered words, be restrained in speech. Giving up bad verbal conduct, conduct yourself well in speech.
passages.title: Dhammapada 232 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Vacīpakopaṁ rakkheyya,  vācāya saṁvuto siyā;  Vacīduccaritaṁ hitvā,  vācāya sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: Guard against ill-tempered thoughts, be restrained in mind. Giving up bad mental conduct, conduct yourself well in mind.
passages.title: Dhammapada 233 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Manopakopaṁ rakkheyya,  manasā saṁvuto siyā;  Manoduccaritaṁ hitvā,  manasā sucaritaṁ care.

passages.text: An attentive one is restrained in body restrained also in speech, in thought, too, they are restrained: they are restrained in every way.
passages.title: Dhammapada 234 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 221–234 · 17. Anger
passages.original: Kāyena saṁvutā dhīrā,  atho vācāya saṁvutā;  Manasā saṁvutā dhīrā,  te ve suparisaṁvutā.

passages.text: Today you’re like a withered leaf, Yama’s men await you. You stand at the departure gates, yet you have no supplies for the road.
passages.title: Dhammapada 235 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Paṇḍupalāsova dānisi,  Yamapurisāpi ca te upaṭṭhitā;  Uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi,  Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.

passages.text: Make an island of yourself! Swiftly strive, learn to be wise! Purged of stains, flawless, you’ll go to the heavenly realm of the noble ones.
passages.title: Dhammapada 236 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: So karohi dīpamattano,  Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava;  Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo,  Dibbaṁ ariyabhūmiṁ upehisi.

passages.text: You’ve journeyed the stages of life, and now you set out to meet Yama. Along the way there’s nowhere to stay, yet you have no supplies for the road.
passages.title: Dhammapada 237 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Upanītavayo ca dānisi,  Sampayātosi yamassa santikaṁ;  Vāso te natthi antarā,  Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.

passages.text: Make an island of yourself! Swiftly strive, learn to be wise! Purged of stains, flawless, you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
passages.title: Dhammapada 238 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: So karohi dīpamattano,  Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava;  Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo,  Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.

passages.text: A smart person would purge their own stains gradually, bit by bit, moment by moment, like a smith smelting silver.
passages.title: Dhammapada 239 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Anupubbena medhāvī,  thokaṁ thokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe;  Kammāro rajatasseva,  niddhame malamattano.

passages.text: It is the rust born on the iron that eats away the place it arose. And so it is their own deeds that lead the overly-ascetic to a bad place.
passages.title: Dhammapada 240 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Ayasāva malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ,  Tatuṭṭhāya tameva khādati;  Evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ,  Sāni kammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Not rehearsing is the stain of hymns. The stain of houses is neglect. Laziness is the stain of beauty. A guard’s stain is negligence.
passages.title: Dhammapada 241 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Asajjhāyamalā mantā,  anuṭṭhānamalā gharā;  Malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ,  pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.

passages.text: Misconduct is a woman’s stain. A giver’s stain is stinginess. Bad qualities are a stain in this world and the next.
passages.title: Dhammapada 242 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Malitthiyā duccaritaṁ,  maccheraṁ dadato malaṁ;  Malā ve pāpakā dhammā,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.

passages.text: But a worse stain than these is ignorance, the worst stain of all. Having given up that stain, be without stains, mendicants!
passages.title: Dhammapada 243 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Tato malā malataraṁ,  avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ;  Etaṁ malaṁ pahantvāna,  nimmalā hotha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: Life is easy for the shameless. With all the rude courage of a crow, they live pushy, rude, and corrupt.
passages.title: Dhammapada 244 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena,  kākasūrena dhaṁsinā;  Pakkhandinā pagabbhena,  saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.

passages.text: Life is hard for the conscientious, always seeking purity, neither clinging nor rude, pure of livelihood and discerning.
passages.title: Dhammapada 245 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ,  niccaṁ sucigavesinā;  Alīnenāppagabbhena,  suddhājīvena passatā.

passages.text: Take anyone in this world who kills living creatures, speaks falsely, steals, commits adultery,
passages.title: Dhammapada 246 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Yo pāṇamatipāteti,  musāvādañca bhāsati;  Loke adinnamādiyati,  paradārañca gacchati.

passages.text: and indulges in drinking beer and wine. Right here they dig up the root of their own self.
passages.title: Dhammapada 247 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Surāmerayapānañca,  yo naro anuyuñjati;  Idheva meso lokasmiṁ,  mūlaṁ khaṇati attano.

passages.text: Know this, my man: they are unrestrained and wicked. Don’t let that greed and unrighteousness inflict pain on you for long.
passages.title: Dhammapada 248 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Evaṁ bho purisa jānāhi,  pāpadhammā asaññatā;  Mā taṁ lobho adhammo ca,  ciraṁ dukkhāya randhayuṁ.

passages.text: The people give according to their faith, according to their confidence. If you get upset over that, over others’ food and drink, you’ll not, by day or by night, become immersed in samādhi.
passages.title: Dhammapada 249 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ,  yathāpasādanaṁ jano;  Tattha yo ca maṅku bhavati,  paresaṁ pānabhojane;  Na so divā vā rattiṁ vā,  samādhimadhigacchati.

passages.text: Those who have cut that out, dug it up at the root, eradicated it, they will, by day or by night, become immersed in samādhi.
passages.title: Dhammapada 250 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ,  mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ;  Sa ve divā vā rattiṁ vā,  samādhimadhigacchati.

passages.text: There is no fire like greed, no crime like hate, no net like delusion, no river like craving.
passages.title: Dhammapada 251 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Natthi rāgasamo aggi,  natthi dosasamo gaho;  Natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ,  natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.

passages.text: It’s easy to see the faults of others, hard to see one’s own. For the faults of others are tossed high like hay, while one’s own are hidden, as a cheat hides a bad hand.
passages.title: Dhammapada 252 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Sudassaṁ vajjamaññesaṁ,  attano pana duddasaṁ;  Paresaṁ hi so vajjāni,  opunāti yathā bhusaṁ;  Attano pana chādeti,  kaliṁva kitavā saṭho.

passages.text: When you look for the flaws of others, always finding fault, your defilements only grow, you’re far from ending defilements.
passages.title: Dhammapada 253 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Paravajjānupassissa,  niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino;  Āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti,  ārā so āsavakkhayā.

passages.text: In the atmosphere there is no track, there’s no true ascetic outside here. People enjoy proliferation, the Realized Ones are free of proliferation.
passages.title: Dhammapada 254 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi,  samaṇo natthi bāhire;  Papañcābhiratā pajā,  nippapañcā tathāgatā.

passages.text: In the atmosphere there is no track, there’s no true ascetic outside here. No conditions last forever, the Awakened Ones are not shaken.
passages.title: Dhammapada 255 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 235–255 · 18. Stains
passages.original: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi,  samaṇo natthi bāhire;  Saṅkhārā sassatā natthi,  natthi buddhānamiñjitaṁ.

passages.text: You don’t become just by passing hasty judgment. An astute person evaluates both what is pertinent and what is irrelevant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 256 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tena hoti dhammaṭṭho,  yenatthaṁ sāhasā naye;  Yo ca atthaṁ anatthañca,  ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.

passages.text: A wise one judges others without haste, justly and impartially; that guardian of the law is said to be just.
passages.title: Dhammapada 257 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Asāhasena dhammena,  samena nayatī pare;  Dhammassa gutto medhāvī,  “dhammaṭṭho”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: You’re not an astute scholar just because you speak a lot. One who is secure, free of enmity and fear, is said to be astute.
passages.title: Dhammapada 258 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tena paṇḍito hoti,  yāvatā bahu bhāsati;  Khemī averī abhayo,  “paṇḍito”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: You’re not one who has memorized the teaching just because you recite a lot. Someone who directly sees the teaching after hearing only a little is truly one who has memorized the teaching, for they can never forget it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 259 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tāvatā dhammadharo,  yāvatā bahu bhāsati;  Yo ca appampi sutvāna,  dhammaṁ kāyena passati;  Sa ve dhammadharo hoti,  yo dhammaṁ nappamajjati.

passages.text: You don’t become a senior by getting some grey hairs; for one ripe only in age, is said to have aged in vain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 260 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tena thero so hoti,  yenassa palitaṁ siro;  Paripakko vayo tassa,  “moghajiṇṇo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: One who is truthful and principled, harmless, restrained, and self-controlled, attentive, purged of stains, is said to be a senior.
passages.title: Dhammapada 261 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca,  ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo;  Sa ve vantamalo dhīro,  “thero” iti pavuccati.

passages.text: Not by mere enunciation, or a beautiful complexion does a person become holy, if they’re jealous, stingy, and devious.
passages.title: Dhammapada 262 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na vākkaraṇamattena,  vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā;  Sādhurūpo naro hoti,  issukī maccharī saṭho.

passages.text: But if they’ve cut that out, dug it up at the root, eradicated it, that intelligent one, purged of vice, is said to be holy.
passages.title: Dhammapada 263 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ,  mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ;  Sa vantadoso medhāvī,  “sādhurūpo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: A liar and breaker of vows is no ascetic just because they shave their head. How on earth can one be an ascetic who’s full of desire and greed?
passages.title: Dhammapada 264 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo,  abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ;  Icchālobhasamāpanno,  samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati.

passages.text: One who stops all wicked deeds, great and small, because of stopping wicked deeds is said to be an ascetic.
passages.title: Dhammapada 265 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Yo ca sameti pāpāni,  aṇuṁthūlāni sabbaso;  Samitattā hi pāpānaṁ,  “samaṇo”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: You don’t become a mendicant just by begging from others. One who has undertaken domestic duties has not yet become a mendicant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 266 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tena bhikkhu so hoti,  yāvatā bhikkhate pare;  Vissaṁ dhammaṁ samādāya,  bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.

passages.text: But one living a spiritual life, who has banished both merit and evil, who wanders having appraised the world, is said to be a mendicant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 267 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Yodha puññañca pāpañca,  bāhetvā brahmacariyavā;  Saṅkhāya loke carati,  sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.

passages.text: You don’t become a sage by being sagelike, while still confused and ignorant. The astute one who holds the scales, taking only the best,
passages.title: Dhammapada 268 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na monena munī hoti,  mūḷharūpo aviddasu;  Yo ca tulaṁva paggayha,  varamādāya paṇḍito.

passages.text: and shunning the bad— that is a sage, and that is how one becomes a sage. One who sagely weighs both in the world, is thereby said to be a sage.
passages.title: Dhammapada 269 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Pāpāni parivajjeti,  sa munī tena so muni;  Yo munāti ubho loke,  “muni” tena pavuccati.

passages.text: You don’t become a noble one by harming living beings. One harmless toward all living beings is said to be a noble one.
passages.title: Dhammapada 270 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na tena ariyo hoti,  yena pāṇāni hiṁsati;  Ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ,  “ariyo”ti pavuccati.

passages.text: Not by precepts and observances, nor by much learning, nor by meditative immersion, nor by living in seclusion,
passages.title: Dhammapada 271 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Na sīlabbatamattena,  bāhusaccena vā pana;  Atha vā samādhilābhena,  vivittasayanena vā.

passages.text: do I experience the bliss of renunciation not frequented by ordinary people. A mendicant cannot rest confident without attaining the end of defilements.
passages.title: Dhammapada 272 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 256–272 · 19. The Just
passages.original: Phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ,  aputhujjanasevitaṁ;  Bhikkhu vissāsamāpādi,  appatto āsavakkhayaṁ.
