passages.text: Of paths, the eightfold is the best; of truths, the four statements; dispassion is the best of things, and the Clear-eyed One is the best of humans.
passages.title: Dhammapada 273 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho,  saccānaṁ caturo padā;  Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ,  dvipadānañca cakkhumā.

passages.text: This is the path, there is no other for the purification of vision. You all must practice this, it is the way to baffle Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 274 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Eseva maggo natthañño,  Dassanassa visuddhiyā;  Etañhi tumhe paṭipajjatha,  Mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.

passages.text: When you all are practicing this, you’ll make an end of suffering. I have explained the path to you for extracting the thorn with wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 275 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Etañhi tumhe paṭipannā,  dukkhassantaṁ karissatha;  Akkhāto vo mayā maggo,  aññāya sallakantanaṁ.

passages.text: You yourselves must do the work, the Realized Ones just show the way. Meditators practicing absorption are released from Māra’s bonds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 276 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Tumhehi kiccamātappaṁ,  akkhātāro tathāgatā;  Paṭipannā pamokkhanti,  jhāyino mārabandhanā.

passages.text: All conditions are impermanent— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 277 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: “Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: All conditions are suffering— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 278 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: “Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: All things are not-self— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 279 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: “Sabbe dhammā anattā”ti,  yadā paññāya passati;  Atha nibbindati dukkhe,  esa maggo visuddhiyā.

passages.text: They don’t get going when it’s time to start; they’re young and strong, but given to sloth. Their mind depressed in sunken thought, lazy and slothful, they can’t discern the path.
passages.title: Dhammapada 280 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno,  Yuvā balī ālasiyaṁ upeto;  Saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto,  Paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.

passages.text: Guarded in speech, restrained in mind, doing no unskillful bodily deed. Purify these three ways of performing deeds, and win the path known to seers.
passages.title: Dhammapada 281 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto,  Kāyena ca nākusalaṁ kayirā;  Ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye,  Ārādhaye maggamisippaveditaṁ.

passages.text: From meditation springs wisdom, without meditation, wisdom ends. Knowing these two paths— of progress and decline— you should conduct yourself so that wisdom grows.
passages.title: Dhammapada 282 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri,  ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo;  Etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā,  bhavāya vibhavāya ca;  Tathāttānaṁ niveseyya,  yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Cut down the jungle, not just a tree; from the jungle springs fear. Having cut down jungle and snarl, be free of jungles, mendicants!
passages.title: Dhammapada 283 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ,  vanato jāyate bhayaṁ;  Chetvā vanañca vanathañca,  nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: So long as the vine, no matter how small, that ties a man to women is not cut, his mind remains trapped, like a calf suckling its mother.
passages.title: Dhammapada 284 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Yāva hi vanatho na chijjati,  Aṇumattopi narassa nārisu;  Paṭibaddhamanova tāva so,  Vaccho khīrapakova mātari.

passages.text: Cut out affection for oneself, like plucking an autumn lotus. Foster only the path to peace, the extinguishment the Holy One taught.
passages.title: Dhammapada 285 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Ucchinda sinehamattano,  Kumudaṁ sāradikaṁva pāṇinā;  Santimaggameva brūhaya,  Nibbānaṁ sugatena desitaṁ.

passages.text: “Here I will stay for the rains; here for winter, here the summer”; thus the fool thinks, not realizing the danger.
passages.title: Dhammapada 286 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Idha vassaṁ vasissāmi,  idha hemantagimhisu;  Iti bālo vicinteti,  antarāyaṁ na bujjhati.

passages.text: As a mighty flood sweeps away a sleeping village, death steals away a man who dotes on children and cattle, his mind caught up in them.
passages.title: Dhammapada 287 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova,  maccu ādāya gacchati.

passages.text: Children provide you no shelter, nor does father, nor relatives. When you’re seized by the terminator, there’s no shelter in family.
passages.title: Dhammapada 288 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Na santi puttā tāṇāya,  na pitā nāpi bandhavā;  Antakenādhipannassa,  natthi ñātīsu tāṇatā.

passages.text: Knowing the reason for this, astute, and ethically restrained, one would quickly clear the path that leads to extinguishment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 289 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 273–289 · 20. The Path
passages.original: Etamatthavasaṁ ñatvā,  paṇḍito sīlasaṁvuto;  Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ,  khippameva visodhaye.

passages.text: If by giving up material happiness one sees abundant happiness, the attentive would give up material happiness, seeing the abundant happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 290 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Mattāsukhapariccāgā,  passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ;  Caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro,  sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Seeking their own happiness by imposing suffering on others, intimate with enmity, they’re not freed from enmity.
passages.title: Dhammapada 291 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Paradukkhūpadhānena,  attano sukhamicchati;  Verasaṁsaggasaṁsaṭṭho,  verā so na parimuccati.

passages.text: They dump what should be done, and do what should not be done. For the insolent and the negligent, their defilements only grow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 292 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Yañhi kiccaṁ apaviddhaṁ,  akiccaṁ pana karīyati;  Unnaḷānaṁ pamattānaṁ,  tesaṁ vaḍḍhanti āsavā.

passages.text: Those that have properly undertaken constant mindfulness of the body, don’t cultivate what should not be done, but always do what should be done. Mindful and aware, their defilements come to an end.
passages.title: Dhammapada 293 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Yesañca susamāraddhā,  niccaṁ kāyagatā sati;  Akiccaṁ te na sevanti,  kicce sātaccakārino;  Satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ,  atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.

passages.text: Having slain mother and father, and two aristocratic kings, and having wiped out the kingdom with its tax collector, the brahmin walks on untroubled.
passages.title: Dhammapada 294 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā,  rājāno dve ca khattiye;  Raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā,  anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: Having slain mother and father, and two prosperous kings, and a tiger as the fifth, the brahmin walks on untroubled.
passages.title: Dhammapada 295 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā,  rājāno dve ca sotthiye;  Veyagghapañcamaṁ hantvā,  anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Buddha.
passages.title: Dhammapada 296 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ buddhagatā sati.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 297 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ dhammagatā sati.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Saṅgha.
passages.title: Dhammapada 298 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ saṅghagatā sati.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night are constantly mindful of the body.
passages.title: Dhammapada 299 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  niccaṁ kāyagatā sati.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in harmlessness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 300 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  ahiṁsāya rato mano.

passages.text: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in meditation.
passages.title: Dhammapada 301 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti,  sadā gotamasāvakā;  Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca,  bhāvanāya rato mano.

passages.text: Going forth is hard, it’s hard to be happy; life at home is hard too, and painful, it’s painful to stay when you’ve nothing in common. A traveler is a prey to pain, so don’t be a traveler, don’t be prey to pain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 302 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ,  Durāvāsā gharā dukhā;  Dukkhosamānasaṁvāso,  Dukkhānupatitaddhagū;  Tasmā na caddhagū siyā,  Na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.

passages.text: One who is faithful, accomplished in ethics, blessed with fame and wealth, is honored in whatever place they frequent.
passages.title: Dhammapada 303 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Saddho sīlena sampanno,  yasobhogasamappito;  Yaṁ yaṁ padesaṁ bhajati,  tattha tattheva pūjito.

passages.text: The good shine from afar, like the Himalayan peaks, but the wicked are not seen, like arrows scattered in the night.
passages.title: Dhammapada 304 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Dūre santo pakāsenti,  himavantova pabbato;  Asantettha na dissanti,  rattiṁ khittā yathā sarā.

passages.text: Sitting alone, sleeping alone, tirelessly wandering alone; one who tames themselves alone would delight within a forest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 305 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 290–305 · 21. Miscellaneous
passages.original: Ekāsanaṁ ekaseyyaṁ,  eko caramatandito;  Eko damayamattānaṁ,  vanante ramito siyā.

passages.text: A liar goes to hell, as does one who denies what they did. Both are equal in the hereafter, those men of base deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 306 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Abhūtavādī nirayaṁ upeti,  Yo vāpi katvā na karomi cāha;  Ubhopi te pecca samā bhavanti,  Nihīnakammā manujā parattha.

passages.text: Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth are unrestrained and wicked. Being wicked, they are reborn in hell due to their bad deeds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 307 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo,  pāpadhammā asaññatā;  Pāpā pāpehi kammehi,  nirayaṁ te upapajjare.

passages.text: It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained to eat an iron ball, scorching, like a burning flame, than to eat the nation’s alms.
passages.title: Dhammapada 308 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto,  tatto aggisikhūpamo;  Yañce bhuñjeyya dussīlo,  raṭṭhapiṇḍamasaññato.

passages.text: Four things befall a heedless man who sleeps with another’s wife: wickedness, poor sleep, ill-repute, and rebirth in hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 309 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto,  Āpajjati paradārūpasevī;  Apuññalābhaṁ na nikāmaseyyaṁ,  Nindaṁ tatīyaṁ nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.

passages.text: He accrues wickedness and is reborn in a bad place, all so a frightened couple may snatch a moment’s pleasure, for which rulers impose a heavy punishment. That’s why a man should not sleep with another’s wife.
passages.title: Dhammapada 310 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā,  Bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā;  Rājā ca daṇḍaṁ garukaṁ paṇeti,  Tasmā naro paradāraṁ na seve.

passages.text: When kusa grass is wrongly grasped it only cuts the hand. So too, the ascetic life, when wrongly taken, drags you to hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 311 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Kuso yathā duggahito,  hatthamevānukantati;  Sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ,  nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.

passages.text: Any lax act, any corrupt observance, or suspicious spiritual life, is not very fruitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 312 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ,  saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṁ vataṁ;  Saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ,  na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: If one is to do what should be done, one should staunchly strive. For the life gone forth when laxly led just stirs up dust all the more.
passages.title: Dhammapada 313 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ,  daḷhamenaṁ parakkame;  Sithilo hi paribbājo,  bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.

passages.text: A bad deed is better left undone, for it will plague you later on. A good deed is better done, one that does not plague you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 314 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Akataṁ dukkaṭaṁ seyyo,  pacchā tappati dukkaṭaṁ;  Katañca sukataṁ seyyo,  yaṁ katvā nānutappati.

passages.text: As a frontier city is guarded inside and out, so you should ward yourselves— don’t let the moment pass you by. For if you miss your moment you’ll grieve when sent to hell.
passages.title: Dhammapada 315 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ,  guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ;  Evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ,  khaṇo vo mā upaccagā;  Khaṇātītā hi socanti,  nirayamhi samappitā.

passages.text: Unashamed of what is shameful, ashamed of what is not shameful; beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
passages.title: Dhammapada 316 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Alajjitāye lajjanti,  lajjitāye na lajjare;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Seeing danger where there is none, and blind to the actual danger, beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
passages.title: Dhammapada 317 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Abhaye bhayadassino,  bhaye cābhayadassino;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Seeing fault where there is none, and blind to the actual fault, beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
passages.title: Dhammapada 318 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Avajje vajjamatino,  vajje cāvajjadassino;  Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.

passages.text: Knowing a fault as a fault and the faultless as faultless, beings who uphold right view go to a good place.
passages.title: Dhammapada 319 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 306–319 · 22. Hell
passages.original: Vajjañca vajjato ñatvā,  avajjañca avajjato;  Sammādiṭṭhisamādānā,  sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.

passages.text: Like an elephant struck with arrows in battle, I shall endure abuse, for so many folk are badly behaved.
passages.title: Dhammapada 320 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Ahaṁ nāgova saṅgāme,  cāpato patitaṁ saraṁ;  Ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ,  dussīlo hi bahujjano.

passages.text: The well-tamed beast is the one led to the crowd; the tamed elephant’s the one the king mounts; the tamed person who endures abuse is the best of human beings.
passages.title: Dhammapada 321 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ,  dantaṁ rājābhirūhati;  Danto seṭṭho manussesu,  yotivākyaṁ titikkhati.

passages.text: Those who have tamed themselves are better than fine tamed mules, thoroughbreds from Sindh, or giant tuskers.
passages.title: Dhammapada 322 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Varamassatarā dantā,  ājānīyā ca sindhavā;  Kuñjarā ca mahānāgā,  attadanto tato varaṁ.

passages.text: For not on those mounts would you go to the untrodden place, whereas, with the help of one whose self is well tamed, you go there, tamed by the tamed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 323 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Na hi etehi yānehi,  gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ;  Yathāttanā sudantena,  danto dantena gacchati.

passages.text: The tusker named Dhanapāla is musky in rut, hard to control. Bound, he eats not a morsel, for he misses the elephant forest.
passages.title: Dhammapada 324 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Dhanapālo nāma kuñjaro,  Kaṭukabhedano dunnivārayo;  Baddho kabaḷaṁ na bhuñjati,  Sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.

passages.text: One who gets drowsy from overeating, fond of sleep, rolling round the bed like a great hog stuffed with grain: that dullard returns to the womb again and again.
passages.title: Dhammapada 325 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca,  Niddāyitā samparivattasāyī;  Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho,  Punappunaṁ gabbhamupeti mando.

passages.text: In the past my mind wandered how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased. Now I’ll carefully guide it, as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 326 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Idaṁ pure cittamacāri cārikaṁ,  Yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ;  Tadajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso,  Hatthippabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.

passages.text: Delight in diligence! Take good care of your mind! Pull yourself out of this pit, like an elephant sunk in a bog.
passages.title: Dhammapada 327 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Appamādaratā hotha,  sacittamanurakkhatha;  Duggā uddharathattānaṁ,  paṅke sannova kuñjaro.

passages.text: If you find an alert companion, an attentive friend to live happily together, then, overcoming all adversities, wander with them, joyful and mindful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 328 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ,  Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ;  Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni,  Careyya tenattamano satīmā.

passages.text: If you find no alert companion, no attentive friend to live happily together, then, like a king who flees his conquered realm, wander alone like a tusker in the wilds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 329 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ,  Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ;  Rājāva raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya,  Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.

passages.text: It’s better to wander alone, there’s no fellowship with fools. Wander alone and do no wrong, at ease like a tusker in the wilds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 330 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo,  Natthi bāle sahāyatā;  Eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā,  Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.

passages.text: A friend in need is a blessing; it’s a blessing to be content with whatever; good deeds are a blessing at the end of life, and giving up all suffering is a blessing.
passages.title: Dhammapada 331 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā,  Tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena;  Puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi,  Sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahānaṁ.

passages.text: In this world it’s a blessing to serve one’s mother and one’s father. And it’s a blessing also to serve ascetics and brahmins.
passages.title: Dhammapada 332 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Sukhā matteyyatā loke,  atho petteyyatā sukhā;  Sukhā sāmaññatā loke,  atho brahmaññatā sukhā.

passages.text: It’s a blessing to keep precepts until you grow old; a blessing to be grounded in faith; the getting of wisdom’s a blessing; and it’s a blessing to avoid doing wrong.
passages.title: Dhammapada 333 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 320–333 · 23. Elephants
passages.original: Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ,  sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā;  Sukho paññāya paṭilābho,  pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: The mind quivers and quakes, hard to guard, hard to curb. The discerning straighten it out, like a fletcher an arrow.
passages.title: Dhammapada 33 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ,  dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ;  Ujuṁ karoti medhāvī,  usukārova tejanaṁ.

passages.text: Like a fish pulled from the sea and cast upon the shore, this mind flounders about, trying to throw off Māra’s dominion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 34 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Vārijova thale khitto,  okamokataubbhato;  Pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ,  māradheyyaṁ pahātave.

passages.text: Hard to hold back, flighty, alighting where it will; it’s good to tame the mind; a tamed mind leads to bliss.
passages.title: Dhammapada 35 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Dunniggahassa lahuno,  yatthakāmanipātino;  Cittassa damatho sādhu,  cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.

passages.text: So hard to see, so subtle, alighting where it will; the discerning protect the mind, a guarded mind leads to bliss.
passages.title: Dhammapada 36 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ,  yatthakāmanipātinaṁ;  Cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī,  cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.

passages.text: The mind travels far, wandering alone; incorporeal, it lies hidden in the heart. Those who will restrain the mind are freed from Māra’s bonds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 37 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ,  asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ;  Ye cittaṁ saṁyamissanti,  mokkhanti mārabandhanā.

passages.text: Those of unsteady mind, who don’t understand the true teaching, and whose confidence wavers, do not perfect their wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 38 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa,  saddhammaṁ avijānato;  Pariplavapasādassa,  paññā na paripūrati.

passages.text: One whose mind is not festering, whose heart is undamaged, who’s given up right and wrong, alert, has nothing to fear.
passages.title: Dhammapada 39 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Anavassutacittassa,  ananvāhatacetaso;  Puññapāpapahīnassa,  natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.

passages.text: Knowing this body breaks like a pot, and fortifying the mind like a citadel, attack Māra with the sword of wisdom, guard your conquest, and never settle.
passages.title: Dhammapada 40 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā,  Nagarūpamaṁ cittamidaṁ ṭhapetvā;  Yodhetha māraṁ paññāvudhena,  Jitañca rakkhe anivesano siyā.

passages.text: All too soon this body will lie upon the earth, bereft of consciousness, tossed aside like a worthless log.
passages.title: Dhammapada 41 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo,  pathaviṁ adhisessati;  Chuddho apetaviññāṇo,  niratthaṁva kaliṅgaraṁ.

passages.text: A wrongly directed mind would do you more harm than a hater to the hated, or an enemy to their foe.
passages.title: Dhammapada 42 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā,  verī vā pana verinaṁ;  Micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ,  pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.

passages.text: A rightly directed mind would do you more good than your mother or father or any other relative.
passages.title: Dhammapada 43 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 33–43 · 3. The Mind
passages.original: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā,  aññe vāpi ca ñātakā;  Sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ,  seyyaso naṁ tato kare.

passages.text: When a man lives heedlessly, craving grows in them like a camel’s foot creeper. They jump from one thing to the next, like a langur greedy for fruit in a forest grove.
passages.title: Dhammapada 334 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Manujassa pamattacārino,  Taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya;  So plavatī hurā huraṁ,  Phalamicchaṁva vanasmi vānaro.

passages.text: Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving, this attachment to the world, their sorrow grows, like grass in the rain.
passages.title: Dhammapada 335 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Yaṁ esā sahate jammī,  taṇhā loke visattikā;  Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti,  abhivaṭṭhaṁva bīraṇaṁ.

passages.text: But whoever prevails over this wretched craving, so hard to get over in the world, their sorrows fall from them, like a drop from a lotus-leaf.
passages.title: Dhammapada 336 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Yo cetaṁ sahate jammiṁ,  taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ;  Sokā tamhā papatanti,  udabinduva pokkharā.

passages.text: I say this to you, good people, all those who have gathered here: dig up the root of craving, as you’d dig up grass in search of roots. Don’t let Māra break you again and again, like a stream breaking a reed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 337 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Taṁ vo vadāmi bhaddaṁ vo,  yāvantettha samāgatā;  Taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha,  usīratthova bīraṇaṁ;  Mā vo naḷaṁva sotova,  māro bhañji punappunaṁ.

passages.text: A tree grows back even when cut down, so long as its roots are strong and undamaged; suffering springs up again and again, so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out.
passages.title: Dhammapada 338 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Yathāpi mūle anupaddave daḷhe,  Chinnopi rukkho punareva rūhati;  Evampi taṇhānusaye anūhate,  Nibbattatī dukkhamidaṁ punappunaṁ.

passages.text: A person of low views in whom the thirty-six streams that flow to pleasure are mighty, is swept away by lustful thoughts.
passages.title: Dhammapada 339 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Yassa chattiṁsati sotā,  manāpasavanā bhusā;  Mahāvahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ,  saṅkappā rāganissitā.

passages.text: The streams flow everywhere; a weed springs up and remains. Seeing this weed that has been born, cut the root with wisdom.
passages.title: Dhammapada 340 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Savanti sabbadhi sotā,  latā uppajja tiṭṭhati;  Tañca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ,  mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha.

passages.text: A personage’s joys flow from senses and cravings. Seekers of happiness, bent on pleasure, continue to be reborn and grow old.
passages.title: Dhammapada 341 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Saritāni sinehitāni ca,  Somanassāni bhavanti jantuno;  Te sātasitā sukhesino,  Te ve jātijarūpagā narā.

passages.text: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. Bound and fettered, for a long time they return to pain time and again.
passages.title: Dhammapada 342 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā,  Parisappanti sasova bandhito;  Saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā,  Dukkhamupenti punappunaṁ cirāya.

passages.text: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. That’s why one who longs for dispassion should dispel thirst.
passages.title: Dhammapada 343 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā,  Parisappanti sasova bandhito;  Tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye,  Ākaṅkhanta virāgamattano.

passages.text: Unsnarled, they set out for the jungle, then they run right back to the jungle they left behind. Just look at this individual! Freed, they run to bondage.
passages.title: Dhammapada 344 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto,  Vanamutto vanameva dhāvati;  Taṁ puggalametha passatha,  Mutto bandhanameva dhāvati.

passages.text: The attentive say that shackle is not strong that’s made of iron, wood, or knots. But obsession with jeweled earrings, concern for your partners and children:
passages.title: Dhammapada 345 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,  Yadāyasaṁ dārujapabbajañca;  Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu,  Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā.

passages.text: this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape. Having cut this one too they go forth, unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures.
passages.title: Dhammapada 346 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,  Ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ duppamuñcaṁ;  Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti,  Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṁ pahāya.

passages.text: Besotted by lust they fall into the stream, like a spider caught in the web she wove. The attentive proceed, having cut this one too, unconcerned, having given up all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 347 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ,  Sayaṅkataṁ makkaṭakova jālaṁ;  Etampi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā,  Anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya.

passages.text: Let go of the past, let go of the future, let go of the present, having gone beyond rebirth. With your heart freed in every respect, you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
passages.title: Dhammapada 348 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Muñca pure muñca pacchato,  Majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū;  Sabbattha vimuttamānaso,  Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.

passages.text: For a personage churned by thoughts, very lustful, focusing on beauty, their craving grows and grows, tying them with a stout bond.
passages.title: Dhammapada 349 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Vitakkamathitassa jantuno,  Tibbarāgassa subhānupassino;  Bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati,  Esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ.

passages.text: But one who loves to calm their thoughts, developing perception of ugliness, ever mindful, will surely eliminate that craving, cutting off the bonds of Māra.
passages.title: Dhammapada 350 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Vitakkūpasame ca yo rato,  Asubhaṁ bhāvayate sadā sato;  Esa kho byanti kāhiti,  Esa checchati mārabandhanaṁ.

passages.text: One who is confident, unafraid, rid of craving, free of blemish, having struck down the arrows flying to future lives, this bag of bones is their last.
passages.title: Dhammapada 351 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Niṭṭhaṅgato asantāsī,  vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo;  Acchindi bhavasallāni,  antimoyaṁ samussayo.

passages.text: Rid of craving, free of grasping, expert in the definition of terms, knowing the correct structure and sequence of syllables, they are said to be one who bears their final body, one of great wisdom, a great person.
passages.title: Dhammapada 352 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Vītataṇho anādāno,  Niruttipadakovido;  Akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ,  Jaññā pubbāparāni ca;  Sa ve “antimasārīro,  Mahāpañño mahāpuriso”ti vuccati.

passages.text: I am the vanquisher of all, the knower of all, unsullied in the midst of all things. I’ve given up all, freed in the ending of craving. Since I know for myself, whose follower should I be?
passages.title: Dhammapada 353 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi,  Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto;  Sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto,  Sayaṁ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṁ.

passages.text: The gift of the teaching surmounts all other gifts; the taste of the teaching surmounts all other tastes; the joy of the teaching surmounts all other joys; the ending of craving surmounts all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 354 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Sabbadānaṁ dhammadānaṁ jināti,  Sabbarasaṁ dhammaraso jināti;  Sabbaratiṁ dhammarati jināti,  Taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.

passages.text: Riches ruin a simpleton, but not a seeker of the far shore. From craving for wealth, a simpleton ruins themselves and others.
passages.title: Dhammapada 355 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ,  no ca pāragavesino;  Bhogataṇhāya dummedho,  hanti aññeva attanaṁ.

passages.text: Weeds are the bane of crops, but greed is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of greed is so very fruitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 356 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītarāgesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Weeds are the bane of crops, but hate is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of hate is so very fruitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 357 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  dosadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītadosesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Weeds are the bane of crops, but delusion is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of delusion is so very fruitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 358 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  mohadosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vītamohesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Weeds are the bane of crops, but desire is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of desire is so very fruitful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 359 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 334–359 · 24. Craving
passages.original: Tiṇadosāni khettāni,  icchādosā ayaṁ pajā;  Tasmā hi vigaticchesu,  dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.

passages.text: Restraint of the eye is good; good is restraint of the ear; restraint of the nose is good; good is restraint of the tongue.
passages.title: Dhammapada 360 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu sotena saṁvaro;  Ghānena saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro.

passages.text: Restraint of the body is good; good is restraint of speech; restraint of mind is good; everywhere, restraint is good. The mendicant restrained everywhere is released from all suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 361 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Kāyena saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu vācāya saṁvaro;  Manasā saṁvaro sādhu,  sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro;  Sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu,  sabbadukkhā pamuccati.

passages.text: One restrained in hand and foot, and in speech, the supreme restraint; happy inside, serene, solitary, content, I call a mendicant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 362 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Hatthasaṁyato pādasaṁyato,  Vācāsaṁyato saṁyatuttamo;  Ajjhattarato samāhito,  Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṁ.

passages.text: When a mendicant of restrained mouth, thoughtful in counsel, not restless, explains the text and its meaning, their words are sweet.
passages.title: Dhammapada 363 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu,  mantabhāṇī anuddhato;  Atthaṁ dhammañca dīpeti,  madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ.

passages.text: Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching, contemplating the teaching, a mendicant who recollects the teaching doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 364 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Dhammārāmo dhammarato,  dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ;  Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu,  saddhammā na parihāyati.

passages.text: A well-off mendicant ought not look down on others, nor should they be envious. A mendicant who envies others does not achieve immersion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 365 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya,  nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care;  Aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu,  samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.

passages.text: If a mendicant is poor in offerings, the well-to-do ought not look down on them. For the gods indeed praise them, who are tireless and pure of livelihood.
passages.title: Dhammapada 366 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Appalābhopi ce bhikkhu,  salābhaṁ nātimaññati;  Taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti,  suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ.

passages.text: One who has no sense of ownership in the whole realm of name and form, who does not grieve for that which is not, is said to be a mendicant.
passages.title: Dhammapada 367 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ,  yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ;  Asatā ca na socati,  sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.

passages.text: A mendicant who meditates on love, devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 368 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu,  pasanno buddhasāsane;  Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ,  saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: Bail out this boat, mendicant! When bailed out it will float lightly. Having cut off desire and hate, you shall reach extinguishment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 369 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ,  sittā te lahumessati;  Chetvā rāgañca dosañca,  tato nibbānamehisi.

passages.text: Five to cut, five to drop, and five more to develop. When a mendicant slips five chains they’re said to have crossed the flood.
passages.title: Dhammapada 370 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Pañca chinde pañca jahe,  pañca cuttari bhāvaye;  Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu,  “oghatiṇṇo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Practice absorption, don’t be negligent! Don’t let the mind delight in the senses! Don’t heedlessly swallow a hot iron ball! And when it burns, don’t cry, “Oh, the pain!”
passages.title: Dhammapada 371 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Jhāya bhikkhu mā pamādo,  Mā te kāmaguṇe ramessu cittaṁ;  Mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī pamatto,  Mā kandi “dukkhamidan”ti dayhamāno.

passages.text: No absorption for one without wisdom, no wisdom for one without absorption. But one with absorption and wisdom— they have truly drawn near to extinguishment.
passages.title: Dhammapada 372 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa,  paññā natthi ajhāyato;  Yamhi jhānañca paññā ca,  sa ve nibbānasantike.

passages.text: A mendicant who enters an empty hut with mind at peace finds a superhuman delight as they rightly discern the Dhamma.
passages.title: Dhammapada 373 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa,  santacittassa bhikkhuno;  Amānusī rati hoti,  sammā dhammaṁ vipassato.

passages.text: Whenever they are mindful of the rise and fall of the aggregates, they feel rapture and joy: that is freedom from death for one who knows.
passages.title: Dhammapada 374 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Yato yato sammasati,  khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ;  Labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ,  amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ.

passages.text: This is the very start of the path for a wise mendicant here: guarding the senses, contentment, and restraint in the monastic code.
passages.title: Dhammapada 375 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Tatrāyamādi bhavati,  idha paññassa bhikkhuno;  Indriyagutti santuṭṭhi,  pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro.

passages.text: Mix with spiritual friends, who are tireless and pure of livelihood. Share what you have with others, being skillful in your conduct. And when you’re full of joy, you’ll make an end to suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 376 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe,  suddhājīve atandite;  Paṭisanthāravutyassa,  ācārakusalo siyā;  Tato pāmojjabahulo,  dukkhassantaṁ karissati.

passages.text: As a jasmine sheds its withered flowers, O mendicants, shed greed and hate.
passages.title: Dhammapada 377 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Vassikā viya pupphāni,  maddavāni pamuñcati;  Evaṁ rāgañca dosañca,  vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.

passages.text: Calm in body, calm in speech, peaceful and serene; a mendicant who’s spat out the world’s bait is said to be one at peace.
passages.title: Dhammapada 378 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Santakāyo santavāco,  santavā susamāhito;  Vantalokāmiso bhikkhu,  “upasanto”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Urge yourself on, reflect on yourself. A mendicant self-controlled and mindful will always dwell in happiness.
passages.title: Dhammapada 379 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Attanā codayattānaṁ,  paṭimaṁsetha attanā;  So attagutto satimā,  sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi.

passages.text: Self is indeed the lord of self, for who else would be one’s lord? Self is indeed the home of self, so restrain yourself, as a merchant his thoroughbred steed.
passages.title: Dhammapada 380 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Attā hi attano nātho,  ko hi nātho paro siyā;  Attā hi attano gati,  tasmā saṁyamamattānaṁ;  Assaṁ bhadraṁva vāṇijo.

passages.text: A monk full of joy trusting in the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 381 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu,  pasanno buddhasāsane;  Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ,  saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.

passages.text: A young mendicant devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, shines upon this world, like the moon freed from clouds.
passages.title: Dhammapada 382 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 360–382 · 25. Mendicants
passages.original: Yo have daharo bhikkhu,  yuñjati buddhasāsane;  Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti,  abbhā muttova candimā.

passages.text: Cut the stream, striving! Cast aside sensual pleasures, brahmin. Knowing the ending of conditions, know the uncreated, brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 383 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma,  kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;  Saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā,  akataññūsi brāhmaṇa.

passages.text: When a brahmin has gone beyond dualistic phenomena, then they consciously make an end of all fetters.
passages.title: Dhammapada 384 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu,  pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo;  Athassa sabbe saṁyogā,  atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.

passages.text: One for whom there is no crossing over or crossing back, or crossing over and back; stress-free, detached, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 385 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā,  pārāpāraṁ na vijjati;  Vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Absorbed, rid of hopes, their task completed, without defilements, arrived at the highest goal: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 386 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Jhāyiṁ virajamāsīnaṁ,  katakiccamanāsavaṁ;  Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: The sun blazes by day, the moon radiates at night, the aristocrat shines in armor, and the brahmin shines in absorption. But all day and all night, the Buddha blazes with glory.
passages.title: Dhammapada 387 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Divā tapati ādicco,  rattimābhāti candimā;  Sannaddho khattiyo tapati,  jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo;  Atha sabbamahorattiṁ,  buddho tapati tejasā.

passages.text: A brahmin’s so-called since they’ve banished evil, an ascetic’s so-called since they live a serene life. One who has renounced all stains is said to be a “renunciant”.
passages.title: Dhammapada 388 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Bāhitapāpoti brāhmaṇo,  Samacariyā samaṇoti vuccati;  Pabbājayamattano malaṁ,  Tasmā “pabbajito”ti vuccati.

passages.text: One should never strike a brahmin, nor should a brahmin retaliate. Woe to the one who hurts a brahmin, and woe for the one who retaliates.
passages.title: Dhammapada 389 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya,  nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo;  Dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ,  tato dhī yassa muñcati.

passages.text: Nothing is better for a brahmin than to hold their mind back from attachment. From wherever a cruel wish recoils, right there suffering subsides.
passages.title: Dhammapada 390 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Na brāhmaṇassetadakiñci seyyo,  Yadā nisedho manaso piyehi;  Yato yato hiṁsamano nivattati,  Tato tato sammatimeva dukkhaṁ.

passages.text: Who does nothing wrong by body, speech or mind, restrained in these three respects, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 391 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassa kāyena vācāya,  manasā natthi dukkaṭaṁ;  Saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: You should graciously honor the one from whom you learn the Dhamma taught by the awakened Buddha, as a brahmin honors the sacred flame.
passages.title: Dhammapada 392 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yamhā dhammaṁ vijāneyya,  sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ;  Sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya,  aggihuttaṁva brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: Not by matted hair or family, or birth is one a brahmin. Those who are truthful and principled: they are pure, they are brahmins.
passages.title: Dhammapada 393 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Na jaṭāhi na gottena,  na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;  Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca,  so sucī so ca brāhmaṇo.

passages.text: Why the matted hair, you simpleton, and why the skin of deer? The tangle is inside you, yet you polish up your outsides.
passages.title: Dhammapada 394 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha,  kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā;  Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ,  bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.

passages.text: A personage who wears robes of rags, lean, their limbs showing veins, meditating alone in the forest, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 395 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ,  kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ;  Ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: I don’t call someone a brahmin after the mother’s womb they’re born from. If they still have attachments, they’re just someone who says “worthy”. Having nothing, taking nothing: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 396 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi,  yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ;  Bhovādi nāma so hoti,  sace hoti sakiñcano;  Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Having cut off all fetters they have no anxiety. They’ve slipped their chains and are detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 397 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Sabbasaṁyojanaṁ chetvā,  yo ve na paritassati;  Saṅgātigaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve cut the strap and harness, the halter and bridle too, with cross-bar lifted, they’re awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 398 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañca,  sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ;  Ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Abuse, killing, caging: they endure these without anger. Patience is their powerful army: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 399 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Akkosaṁ vadhabandhañca,  aduṭṭho yo titikkhati;  Khantībalaṁ balānīkaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Not irritable or pretentious, dutiful in precepts and observances, tamed, bearing their final body: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 400 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Akkodhanaṁ vatavantaṁ,  sīlavantaṁ anussadaṁ;  Dantaṁ antimasārīraṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Like water from a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed off the point of a pin, sensual pleasures slip off them: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 401 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Vāri pokkharapatteva,  āraggeriva sāsapo;  Yo na limpati kāmesu,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They understand for themselves the end of suffering in this life; with burden put down, detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 402 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti,  idheva khayamattano;  Pannabhāraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Deep in wisdom, intelligent, expert in the path and what is not the path; arrived at the highest goal: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 403 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ,  maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ;  Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Mixing with neither householders nor the homeless; a migrant with no bastion, few in wishes: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 404 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi,  anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ;  Anokasārimappicchaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve laid aside violence against creatures firm and frail; not killing or making others kill: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 405 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu,  tasesu thāvaresu ca;  Yo na hanti na ghāteti,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Not fighting among those who fight, quenched among those who have taken up arms, not grasping among those who grasp: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 406 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu,  attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ;  Sādānesu anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve discarded greed and hate, along with conceit and contempt, like a mustard seed off the point of a pin: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 407 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca,  māno makkho ca pātito;  Sāsaporiva āraggā,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: The words they utter are polished, informative, and true, and don’t offend anyone: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 408 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Akakkasaṁ viññāpaniṁ,  giraṁ saccamudīraye;  Yāya nābhisaje kañci,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They don’t steal anything in the world, long or short, tiny or huge, beautiful or ugly: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 409 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā,  aṇuṁ thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ;  Loke adinnaṁ nādiyati,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They have no hope in this world or the next; with no need for hope, detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 410 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Āsā yassa na vijjanti,  asmiṁ loke paramhi ca;  Nirāsāsaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They have no clinging, knowledge has freed them of indecision, they’ve arrived at the objective, freedom from death: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 411 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassālayā na vijjanti,  aññāya akathaṅkathī;  Amatogadhamanuppattaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve escaped the chain of both good and bad deeds; sorrowless, stainless, pure: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 412 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yodha puññañca pāpañca,  ubho saṅgamupaccagā;  Asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Pure as the spotless moon, clear and unclouded, they’ve ended relish for rebirth: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 413 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Candaṁva vimalaṁ suddhaṁ,  vippasannamanāvilaṁ;  Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve got past this grueling swamp of delusion, transmigration. Meditating in stillness, free of indecision, they have crossed over to the far shore. They’re quenched by not grasping: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 414 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yomaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ,  saṁsāraṁ mohamaccagā;  Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī,  anejo akathaṅkathī;  Anupādāya nibbuto,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve given up sensual pleasures, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended rebirth in the sensual realm: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 415 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yodha kāme pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve given up craving, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended craving to be reborn: that’s who I declare a brahmin. They’ve given up craving, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended craving to be reborn: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 416 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.  Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna,  anāgāro paribbaje;  Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They’ve thrown off the human yoke, and slipped out of the heavenly yoke; unyoked from all yokes: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 417 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ,  dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā;  Sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Giving up desire and discontent, they’re cooled and free of attachments; a hero, master of the whole world: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 418 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Hitvā ratiñca aratiñca,  sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ;  Sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They know the passing away and rebirth of all beings; unattached, holy, awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 419 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ,  upapattiñca sabbaso;  Asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Gods, centaurs, and humans don’t know their destiny; the perfected ones with defilements ended: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 420 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti,  devā gandhabbamānusā;  Khīṇāsavaṁ arahantaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: They have nothing before or after, or even in between. Having nothing, taking nothing: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 421 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca,  majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ;  Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: Captain of the herd, excellent hero, great seer and victor; unstirred, washed, awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
passages.title: Dhammapada 422 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ,  mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ;  Anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.

passages.text: One who knows their past lives, sees heaven and places of loss, and has attained the end of rebirth; a sage of perfect insight at the summit of spiritual perfection: that’s who I declare a brahmin. The Sayings of the Dhamma are complete.
passages.title: Dhammapada 423 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 383–423 · 26. Brahmins
passages.original: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedi,  saggāpāyañca passati;  Atho jātikkhayaṁ patto,  abhiññāvosito muni;  Sabbavositavosānaṁ,  tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.  Dhammapadapāḷi samattā.

passages.text: Who bestirs this earth, and the Yama realm with its gods? Who sets out the well-taught word of truth, as an expert a flower?
passages.title: Dhammapada 44 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Ko imaṁ pathaviṁ vicessati,  Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ;  Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ,  Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.

passages.text: A trainee bestirs this earth, and the Yama realm with its gods. A trainee sets out the well-taught word of truth, as an expert a flower.
passages.title: Dhammapada 45 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Sekho pathaviṁ vicessati,  Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ;  Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ,  Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.

passages.text: Knowing this body’s like foam, realizing it’s all just a mirage, and cutting off Māra’s blossoming, vanish from the King of Death.
passages.title: Dhammapada 46 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā,  Marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno;  Chetvāna mārassa papupphakāni,  Adassanaṁ maccurājassa gacche.

passages.text: As a mighty flood sweeps off a sleeping village, death steals away a man even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.
passages.title: Dhammapada 47 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova,  maccu ādāya gacchati.

passages.text: The terminator gains control of the man who has not had his fill of pleasures, even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.
passages.title: Dhammapada 48 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ,  byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ;  Atittaññeva kāmesu,  antako kurute vasaṁ.

passages.text: A bee takes the nectar and moves on, doing no damage to the flower’s beauty and fragrance; and that’s how a sage should walk in the village.
passages.title: Dhammapada 49 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi bhamaro pupphaṁ,  vaṇṇagandhamaheṭhayaṁ;  Paleti rasamādāya,  evaṁ gāme munī care.

passages.text: Don’t find fault with others, with what they’ve done or left undone. You should only watch yourself, what you’ve done or left undone.
passages.title: Dhammapada 50 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Na paresaṁ vilomāni,  na paresaṁ katākataṁ;  Attanova avekkheyya,  katāni akatāni ca.

passages.text: Just like a glorious flower that’s colorful but lacks fragrance; eloquent speech is fruitless for one who does not act on it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 51 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ,  vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ;  Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā,  aphalā hoti akubbato.

passages.text: Just like a glorious flower that’s both colorful and fragrant, eloquent speech is fruitful for one who acts on it.
passages.title: Dhammapada 52 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ,  Vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ;  Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā,  Saphalā hoti kubbato.

passages.text: Just as one would create many garlands from a heap of flowers, when a person has come to be born, they should do many skillful things.
passages.title: Dhammapada 53 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Yathāpi puppharāsimhā,  kayirā mālāguṇe bahū;  Evaṁ jātena maccena,  kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.

passages.text: The fragrance of flowers doesn’t spread upwind, nor sandalwood, pinwheel, or jasmine; but the fragrance of the good spreads upwind; a true person’s virtue spreads in every direction.
passages.title: Dhammapada 54 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Na pupphagandho paṭivātameti,  Na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā;  Satañca gandho paṭivātameti,  Sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.

passages.text: Among all the fragrances— sandalwood or pinwheel or lotus or jasmine— the fragrance of virtue is supreme.
passages.title: Dhammapada 55 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vāpi,  uppalaṁ atha vassikī;  Etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ,  sīlagandho anuttaro.

passages.text: Faint is the fragrance of sandal or pinwheel; but the fragrance of the virtuous floats to the highest gods.
passages.title: Dhammapada 56 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho,  yāyaṁ tagaracandanī;  Yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho,  vāti devesu uttamo.

passages.text: For those accomplished in ethics, meditating diligently, freed through the highest knowledge, Māra cannot find their path.
passages.title: Dhammapada 57 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ,  appamādavihārinaṁ;  Sammadaññāvimuttānaṁ,  māro maggaṁ na vindati.

passages.text: From a heap of trash discarded on the highway, a lotus might blossom, fragrant and delightful.
passages.title: Dhammapada 58 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ,  ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe;  Padumaṁ tattha jāyetha,  sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ.

passages.text: So too, among those thought of as trash, a disciple of the perfect Buddha outshines with their wisdom the blind ordinary folk.
passages.title: Dhammapada 59 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 44–59 · 4. Flowers
passages.original: Evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu,  andhabhūte puthujjane;  Atirocati paññāya,  sammāsambuddhasāvako.

passages.text: Long is the night for the wakeful; long is the league for the weary; long transmigrate the fools who don’t understand the true teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 60 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Dīghā jāgarato ratti,  dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ;  Dīgho bālāna saṁsāro,  saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.

passages.text: If while wandering you find no partner equal or better than yourself, then firmly resolve to wander alone— there’s no fellowship with fools.
passages.title: Dhammapada 61 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Carañce nādhigaccheyya,  Seyyaṁ sadisamattano;  Ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā,  Natthi bāle sahāyatā.

passages.text: “Sons are mine, wealth is mine”— thus the fool frets. For even your self is not your own, let alone your sons or wealth.
passages.title: Dhammapada 62 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Puttā matthi dhanaṁ matthi,  iti bālo vihaññati;  Attā hi attano natthi,  kuto puttā kuto dhanaṁ.

passages.text: The fool who thinks they’re a fool is wise at least to that extent. But the true fool is said to be one who imagines that they are wise.
passages.title: Dhammapada 63 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ,  paṇḍito vāpi tena so;  Bālo ca paṇḍitamānī,  sa ve “bālo”ti vuccati.

passages.text: Though a fool attends to the wise even for the rest of their life, they still don’t understand the teaching, like a spoon the taste of the soup.
passages.title: Dhammapada 64 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Yāvajīvampi ce bālo,  paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati;  Na so dhammaṁ vijānāti,  dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.

passages.text: If a clever person attends to the wise even just for an hour or so, they swiftly understand the teaching, like a tongue the taste of the soup.
passages.title: Dhammapada 65 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Muhuttamapi ce viññū,  paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati;  Khippaṁ dhammaṁ vijānāti,  jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.

passages.text: Fools and simpletons behave like their own worst enemies, doing wicked deeds that ripen as bitter fruit.
passages.title: Dhammapada 66 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Caranti bālā dummedhā,  amitteneva attanā;  Karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ,  yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.

passages.text: It’s not good to do a deed that plagues you later on, for which you weep and wail, as its effect stays with you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 67 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,  yaṁ katvā anutappati;  Yassa assumukho rodaṁ,  vipākaṁ paṭisevati.

passages.text: It is good to do a deed that doesn’t plague you later on, that gladdens and cheers, as its effect stays with you.
passages.title: Dhammapada 68 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Tañca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu,  yaṁ katvā nānutappati;  Yassa patīto sumano,  vipākaṁ paṭisevati.

passages.text: The fool imagines that evil is sweet, so long as it has not yet ripened. But as soon as that evil ripens, they fall into suffering.
passages.title: Dhammapada 69 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Madhuṁvā maññati bālo,  yāva pāpaṁ na paccati;  Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ,  atha dukkhaṁ nigacchati.

passages.text: Month after month a fool may eat food from a grass-blade’s tip; but they’ll never be worth a sixteenth part of one who has appraised the teaching.
passages.title: Dhammapada 70 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Māse māse kusaggena,  bālo bhuñjeyya bhojanaṁ;  Na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ,  kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.

passages.text: For a wicked deed that has been done does not curdle quickly like milk. Smoldering, it follows the fool, like a fire smothered over with ash.
passages.title: Dhammapada 71 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ,  Sajjukhīraṁva muccati;  Ḍahantaṁ bālamanveti,  Bhasmacchannova pāvako.

passages.text: Whatever fame a fool may get, it only gives rise to harm. Whatever good features they have it ruins, and blows their head into bits.
passages.title: Dhammapada 72 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Yāvadeva anatthāya,  ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati;  Hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ,  muddhamassa vipātayaṁ.

passages.text: They’d seek the esteem that they lack, and status among the mendicants; authority over monasteries, and honor among other families.
passages.title: Dhammapada 73 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Asantaṁ bhāvanamiccheyya,  Purekkhārañca bhikkhusu;  Āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ,  Pūjaṁ parakulesu ca.

passages.text: “Let both layfolk and renunciants think the work was done by me alone. In anything at all that’s to be done, let them fall under my sway alone.” So thinks the fool, their greed and pride only growing.
passages.title: Dhammapada 74 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Mameva kata maññantu,  gihī pabbajitā ubho;  Mamevātivasā assu,  kiccākiccesu kismici;  Iti bālassa saṅkappo,  icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.

passages.text: For the means to profit and the path to quenching are two quite different things. A mendicant disciple of the Buddha, understanding what this really means, would never delight in honors, but rather would foster seclusion.
passages.title: Dhammapada 75 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 60–75 · 5. The Fool
passages.original: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā,  aññā nibbānagāminī;  Evametaṁ abhiññāya,  bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;  Sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya,  vivekamanubrūhaye.

passages.text: Regard one who sees your faults as a guide to a hidden treasure. Stay close to one so intelligent and astute who curbs you when you need it. Sticking close to such an impartial person, things get better, not worse.
passages.title: Dhammapada 76 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Nidhīnaṁva pavattāraṁ,  yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ;  Niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ,  tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje;  Tādisaṁ bhajamānassa,  seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.

passages.text: Advise and instruct; curb wickedness: for you shall be loved by the good, and disliked by the bad.
passages.title: Dhammapada 77 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Ovadeyyānusāseyya,  asabbhā ca nivāraye;  Satañhi so piyo hoti,  asataṁ hoti appiyo.

passages.text: Don’t mix with bad friends, nor with the worst of men. Mix with spiritual friends, and with the best of men.
passages.title: Dhammapada 78 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Na bhaje pāpake mitte,  na bhaje purisādhame;  Bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe,  bhajetha purisuttame.

passages.text: Through joy in the teaching you sleep at ease, with clear and confident heart. An astute person always delights in the teaching proclaimed by the Noble One.
passages.title: Dhammapada 79 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti,  vippasannena cetasā;  Ariyappavedite dhamme,  sadā ramati paṇḍito.

passages.text: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, the astute tame themselves.
passages.title: Dhammapada 80 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā,  Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ;  Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā,  Attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: As the wind cannot stir a solid mass of rock, so too blame and praise do not affect the wise.
passages.title: Dhammapada 81 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Selo yathā ekaghano,  vātena na samīrati;  Evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu,  na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: Like a deep lake, clear and unclouded, so clear are the astute when they hear the teachings.
passages.title: Dhammapada 82 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Yathāpi rahado gambhīro,  vippasanno anāvilo;  Evaṁ dhammāni sutvāna,  vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.

passages.text: True persons give up everything, they don’t cajole for the things they desire. Though touched by sadness or happiness, the astute appear neither depressed nor elated.
passages.title: Dhammapada 83 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti,  Na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo;  Sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena,  Na uccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.

passages.text: Never wish for success by unjust means, for your own sake or that of another, desiring children, wealth, or nation; rather, be virtuous, wise, and just.
passages.title: Dhammapada 84 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Na attahetu na parassa hetu,  Na puttamicche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ;  Na iccheyya adhammena samiddhimattano,  Sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.

passages.text: Few are those among humans who cross to the far shore. The rest just run around on the near shore.
passages.title: Dhammapada 85 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Appakā te manussesu,  ye janā pāragāmino;  Athāyaṁ itarā pajā,  tīramevānudhāvati.

passages.text: When the teaching is well explained, the people who practice accordingly will cross over Death’s dominion so hard to pass.
passages.title: Dhammapada 86 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte,  dhamme dhammānuvattino;  Te janā pāramessanti,  maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.

passages.text: Rid of dark qualities, an astute person would develop the bright. Having left home for homelessness in seclusion, where joy is hard,
passages.title: Dhammapada 87 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya,  Sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito;  Okā anokamāgamma,  Viveke yattha dūramaṁ.

passages.text: they’d long for satisfaction there. Forsaking sensual pleasures, owning nothing, an astute person would cleanse themselves of mental corruptions.
passages.title: Dhammapada 88 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Tatrābhiratimiccheyya,  hitvā kāme akiñcano;  Pariyodapeyya attānaṁ,  cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

passages.text: And those whose minds are rightly developed in the awakening factors; who, letting go of attachments, delight in not grasping: with defilements ended, brilliant, they are quenched in this world.
passages.title: Dhammapada 89 · Minor Collection · Sayings of the Dhamma 76–89 · 6. The Astute
passages.original: Yesaṁ sambodhiyaṅgesu,  sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ;  Ādānapaṭinissagge,  anupādāya ye ratā;  Khīṇāsavā jutimanto,  te loke parinibbutā.
